extraction.name: SWE-rebench
extraction.description: A dataset of 21,336 interactive Python-based SWE tasks, suitable for reinforcement learning of SWE agents at scale.
extraction.creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Nebius Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel
extraction.citeAs: Badertdinov et al., SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is collected using a novel, automated, and scalable pipeline to continuously extract real-world interactive SWE tasks from diverse GitHub repositories.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Web Scraping, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The dataset uses continuous supply of fresh tasks collected using SWE-rebench methodology to build a contamination-free benchmark for agentic software engineering.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The primary sources for the data are GitHub Archive and GitHub. The GitHub Archive is a major source of public events on GitHub. Each day, it publishes a JSON archive listing all GitHub events from that day.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The data collection process started before May 1, 2025, and is continuously updated.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: The dataset uses an automated approach to generate candidate environment setup instructions. This process involves several LLM-driven steps: Identifying relevant files, Extracting installation recipe, and Updating the recipe (if needed).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The overall patch is divided into two components: a solution patch, containing changes to non-test files intended to address the issue, and a test patch, comprising only changes to test files.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset undergoes several stages of processing: preliminary task collection, automated installation instruction configuration, execution-based installation verification, and quality assessment.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotations (labels, ratings) are created or authored using a fine-tuned instruction-following model using human annotations from SWE-bench Verified to predict: Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: The platform used to collect annotations by human annotators is not explicitly stated.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The process of converting the "raw" annotations into the final labels involves fine-tuning an instruction-following model using human annotations from SWE-bench Verified.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is continuously updated, and the current set of evaluated models can be found on the leaderboard website. The leaderboard is continuously updated, and the deprecation policies are not explicitly stated.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Any sensitive human attribute(s) collected as part of this dataset include GitHub repository and issue data.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset has the potential to accelerate the development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering. This progress brings potential risks, such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases due to the automated task quality assessment and limited language diversity (initial release is limited exclusively to Python).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The emphasis on scalability introduces trade-offs, particularly a reduced ability to manually curate and verify the quality and clarity of each individual task. The automated task quality assessment may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is suitable for training and evaluating LLM-based software engineering agents, particularly for reinforcement learning-based approaches.
